summary: Defines an initial set of textual conventions, reusable data type definitions, available to all SNMP MIB modules. It was replaced by RFC 2579.

eli5.summary: Instead of explaining what a date or an address looks like every time, this note creates a shared set of ready-made labels that every list can reuse.

questions: what data types do mib modules share
how do you create a row in an snmp table
subtitle: The shared library of named data types, and the RowStatus protocol for creating and deleting table rows, used by SNMPv2 MIB modules.

tldr.problem: MIB authors often want new types that look like the basic SMI types but carry more precise meaning, and without a common set each module would redefine things like MAC addresses and truth values.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1903 defines the TEXTUAL-CONVENTION macro and an initial set of conventions such as DisplayString, MacAddress, TruthValue, RowStatus, TimeStamp, DateAndTime and StorageType. Values are always encoded as their underlying primitive type.
tldr.outcome: The conventions are for the convenience of humans reading MIB modules. RFC 1903 is a Draft Standard that was obsoleted by RFC 2579.

today: RFC 1903 is a Draft Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 2579, which now holds the textual conventions for SNMPv2. It obsoleted RFC 1443.

sections.title: Why Textual Conventions Exist
sections.content:
In SNMP, a MIB is a collection of managed objects, and related objects are grouped in MIB modules written in a subset of ASN.1 called the Structure of Management Information (SMI). When designing a module it is often useful to define a new type with a different name, a similar syntax and a more precise meaning. Such a type is a textual convention.

Textual conventions exist for the convenience of humans reading the MIB module. An object that uses one is always encoded by the rules of its primitive type, so nothing changes on the wire. The ASN.1 macro TEXTUAL-CONVENTION states the syntax and meaning together. Names must be unique and mnemonic and must not exceed 64 characters, although more than 32 characters is not recommended.
sections.eli5: A textual convention is a nickname for a kind of value. The computer still sends the plain value, but people reading the list get a clearer name and meaning.

sections.title: The TEXTUAL-CONVENTION Macro
sections.content:
Each convention has a STATUS (current, deprecated or obsolete), a DESCRIPTION, an optional REFERENCE, an optional DISPLAY-HINT and a SYNTAX. The syntax must be one of the ObjectSyntax alternatives or the BITS construct. The macro expands conceptually during implementation, not at run time. The hyphen is not allowed in the name of a textual convention.

The DISPLAY-HINT may be present only for an underlying INTEGER or OCTET STRING. For integers it picks hexadecimal (x), decimal (d), octal (o) or binary (b), and for decimal it can add an implied decimal point such as d-2, which shows 1234 as 12.34. For octet strings it is a list of octet-format specifications with up to five parts: an optional repeat indicator, an octet length, a display format (x, d, o or a), an optional separator and an optional repeat terminator.
sections.eli5: Each nickname comes with a small form to fill in: what it means, whether it is still in use, and how to show it on a screen.

sections.title: The Basic Conventions
sections.content:
The definitions module, SNMPv2-TC, supplies a set of ready-made types:

  • DisplayString: NVT ASCII text of at most 255 characters.
  • PhysAddress and MacAddress: media-level addresses. A MacAddress is 6 octets in the canonical order of IEEE 802.1a.
  • TruthValue: true(1) or false(2).
  • AutonomousType, VariablePointer and RowPointer: object identifier values, used for extensible type ids and for pointing at an object instance or a table row. InstancePointer is obsolete and replaced by the last two.
  • TimeStamp (the sysUpTime value when something happened) and TimeInterval (units of 0.01 seconds).
  • DateAndTime: 8 or 11 octets with year, month, day, time and optional offset from UTC, for example 1992-5-26,13:30:15.0,-4:0.
  • StorageType: other(1), volatile(2), nonVolatile(3), permanent(4) or readOnly(5).
  • TDomain and TAddress: a kind of transport service and an address in it. For snmpUDPDomain a TAddress is 6 octets, 4 for the IP address and 2 for the UDP port.
sections.eli5: The note hands out a box of ready-made labels: one for yes or no, one for text, one for a date, one for a hardware address, and more.

sections.title: TestAndIncr and RowStatus
sections.content:
TestAndIncr supports atomic operations. A set succeeds only if the supplied value exactly matches the current value, otherwise it fails with inconsistentValue. On success the value is incremented, wrapping to zero after 2147483647.

RowStatus manages the creation and deletion of conceptual table rows. It has six values: active(1), notInService(2), notReady(3), createAndGo(4), createAndWait(5) and destroy(6). The first three are states and can be read; the last three are actions that can be written but never read. A manager can create a row in one set with createAndGo, or negotiate with createAndWait, fill in missing columns, and then set the row to active. Setting destroy deletes the row from any state.

If a manager leaves a row in notInService or notReady the agent must detect it and remove it after an abnormally long time. The text suggests about 5 minutes when the status column does not say otherwise.
sections.eli5: RowStatus is like a sign-up sheet with a few steps. You ask for a new line, fill in the blanks, then say it is ready. If you walk away too long, the clerk crosses the line out.

items.label: active
items.desc: State: the row is available for use by the managed device.

items.label: notInService
items.desc: State: the row exists but is unavailable for use.

items.label: notReady
items.desc: State: the row lacks information needed to be available; readable only.

items.label: createAndGo
items.desc: Action: create the row and make it active at once.

items.label: createAndWait
items.desc: Action: create the row but do not make it available yet.

items.label: destroy
items.desc: Action: delete the row and all its instances.
